newsitem.title: USA: US Air could still face millions in suit.
newsitem.headline: US Air could still face millions in suit.

text.p: US Airways Group Inc could still be faced with millions in damages payments after a federal jury considers how much actual damages it should pay as a result of the 1994 crash of Flight 1016 near Charlotte, attorneys said Friday.

The federal jury on Friday found the company liable for actual, but not punitive, damages in the crash, which left 37 dead and 20 others injured. The ruling means the jury will begin next Wednesday to determine the amount of actual damages to be paid for the deaths.

The trial in Charlotte involved 20 consolidated lawsuits filed against the airline in connection with the crash. On Wednesday, the jury was to begin considering damages in two of those cases and attorneys hoped considering those two would help lead to settlements in the 18 others.
Aviation attorneys said similar awards in commercial aviation cases have typically averaged about $1 million per case, which is covered by carriers' insurance policies.
